title: Session migration ledger reconciliation for resilient streaming metering
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Problem statement: We observe sporadic billing discrepancies after client reconnections, region failovers, and in mid-stream model handoffs. Symptoms include duplicated token debits when a reconnect causes the same output fragment to be reprocessed, and lost credits when server-side session state migrates before all in-flight fragments are reconciled. This ticket specifies a pragmatic reconciliation protocol to make the streaming metering pipeline resilient to session migration, connection failover, and midstream model switches while minimizing runtime overhead and preserving latency SLOs.

Goals:
- Ensure end-to-end token accounting correctness for common migration paths (client reconnect to different proxy, server preemption, model variant fallback).
- Provide idempotent resume semantics that avoid double-charging and avoid missing finalization credits.
- Make reconciliation auditable and debuggable with deterministic anchors and telemetry.

Design summary:
1) Session anchor token: on session creation we mint a short-lived session_anchor_id and include an incremental session_epoch that increments on every server-side handoff (preemption, model switch, proxy failover). The client attaches anchor_id + client_offset (last-received-fragment-index) when resuming.
2) Checkpoint handshake: the server maintains a concise checkpoint summary for each active session_anchor_id: {last_finalized_fragment_index, last_token_tally_checksum, epoch}. The server uses a fast Merkle-style rolling checksum (e.g., BLAKE2s over fragment lengths + token counts) to cheaply validate client offsets without replaying content.
3) Resume algorithm: on resume request, the server compares client_offset and checksum to the stored checkpoint for the matching anchor_id/epoch. If the anchor matches and checksum agreement holds, resume is idempotent: server will not re-debit tokens for fragments <= last_finalized_fragment_index. If mismatched, server falls back to conservative reconciliation where provisional credits are re-evaluated using fragment provenance and a deterministic replay window capped to N fragments to bound CPU cost.
4) Midstream model switch: when model_variant fallback occurs, the serving runtime emits a model_switch_marker into the stream; the checkpoint ledger records a soft boundary so downstream billing aggregates can attribute tokens to the correct variant and apply proration rules.

Trade-offs considered:
- Full event-sourced ledger for every fragment is precise but imposes large storage/IO and increases tail latency. We prefer compact checkpoints + deterministic reconciliation window to keep runtime cost low and still guarantee correctness for >99.9% of migrations.
- Cryptographic checksums vs content hashing: content hashing is heavier; we compute a rolling token-count checksum instead of hashing entire payloads to achieve fast comparisons.

Implementation plan (high level):
- RFC doc: finalize handshake protocol and checksum spec (Confluence link below).
- Runtime: add session_anchor_id and checkpoint summarization to the session manager. Minimal changes to tokenization path to emit fragment token counts into checkpoint builder.
- Billing: extend ledger finalizer to accept epoched checkpoint anchors and idempotency guards. Add fallback path to re-evaluate up to 32 fragments when mismatch detected.
- Proxy: ensure proxy forwards anchor_id on reconnect and returns server guidance when reconciliation is required.
- Tests: unit tests for checksum builder, integration tests for resume scenarios, property-based fuzz tests that simulate reconnects, region failovers, and midstream model switches.
- Shadow run & rollout: feature gated via runtime flag. Shadow-bill a percentage of sessions and compare shadow ledger to production billing for 2 weeks before enabling reconciliation as active protection.

Acceptance criteria:
- Deterministic test harness reproduces previously observed duplication and demonstrates fix eliminates duplicate debits in resume flows.
- Shadow billing delta (fraction of corrected sessions) measurable and below threshold for false-positive re-evaluations.
- New metrics and alerts created (see telemetry section) and dashboards for per-customer orphaned_credit_rate and resume_mismatch_rate.

Telemetry and monitoring:
- meter.resume_mismatch_rate (per 1000 resumes)
- meter.orphaned_credit_rate (orphaned credits per 10k sessions)
- meter.reconciliation_fallback_rate
- billing.delta_tokens_shadow_vs_prod (daily)
- Create SLO: reduce duplicate debit incidents to <1 per 1M sessions within 30 days of rollout.

Rollout plan:
1) Behind feature flag in runtime and ledger finalizer.
2) Canary: enable for internal org + 3 low-volume customers. Monitor metrics and run shadow billing comparison.
3) Expand to 20% of traffic after 72h if no regressions.
4) Full rollout after two weeks of stable telemetry and sign-off from billing and reliability.

Backout plan: revert feature flag and run a compensating audit job to reconcile any sessions where reconciliation incorrectly suppressed legitimate charges.

Security and compliance: session_anchor_id must be unguessable (128-bit random). Any persisted checkpoint summaries are classified as PII-adjacent (could hint at usage patterns) — ensure KMS encryption-at-rest for checkpoint store.

Related work and dependencies: depends on ENG-314159 (clock-skew dedup) for cross-region resume timing heuristics; depends on ENG-612345 (function call tool output metering) for correct attribution when function calls interleave with streaming fragments.

Artifacts and links: see Confluence RFC and experiment notebook.
comments: 2025-02-12 - Aisha Kaur: RFC draft uploaded to Confluence https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/Session+Migration+Metering. Looked for prior art; ENG-314159 has useful clock skew heuristics we should reuse.

2025-02-18 - Ethan Park: Prototype checkpoint builder implemented in runtime session manager. Confirmed negligible CPU cost on microbench, added unit tests for checksum builder (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1234).

2025-02-25 - Design review (Lucas Meyer): Approved design with suggestion to limit fallback replay window to 32 fragments to bound cost. Added UX note: console should surface resume mismatches per customer.

2025-03-01 - Reliability review (Maya Chen): Raised question about multi-proxy reconnection (client may connect to proxy A then B then A). Decided to include epoch monotonicity checks to prevent regressions.

2025-03-03 - QA (Rafael Ortiz): Integration harness added that fuzzes TCP/QUIC reconnects and randomized fragment drop. Found an edge case where fragment index wraps after long sessions; added modulo safety and deterministic tombstone expiry.

2025-03-05 - Ethan Park: Began shadow-billing experiment for internal org traffic. Initial results: meter.resume_mismatch_rate dropped from 12/10k to 0.4/10k in our canary; billing.delta_tokens_shadow_vs_prod shows expected reductions. Link to experiment dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/metrics/session-migration-experiment
